note: Fri 21 Aug 10:10 SGT. TWO-SESSION CATCH-UP covering Wed 19 Aug AND Thu 20 Aug (both complete in Asia+US), plus Friday pre-Asia-open breaking items. The last published edition covered through Tue 18 Aug. Master catalyst this run: the US Treasury's surprise doubling of its long-end debt-buyback operation size (Wed 19 Aug) threads through the gold/silver breakout, the KOSPI round-trip, and the Bitcoin surge — items #1-3 below should be read together. KOSPI's -5.80%-then-+5.89% two-day round trip, flagged for investigation this run, has a citable, dated, two-part explanation (see #2) rather than being an unresolved anomaly.

items.headline: US Treasury doubles long-end bond buybacks — the single biggest cross-asset catalyst of the two sessions
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the Treasury is at least doubling its liquidity-support buyback operations for 10-30yr securities (from $2bn to $4bn per operation), starting 9 Sep, after the 30yr yield hit a post-2007 high (~5.33%) on federal-debt concerns (>$40T). The announcement pulled the 10yr to 4.647% and the 30yr to 5.196%, and was widely read as a return to monetary accommodation.
items.actionable: This buyback is the common thread behind Wed's real gold/silver breakout, Thu's KOSPI rebound, and the Bitcoin surge — a liquidity/debasement trade, not a growth story. Supportive for the silver/gold miners sleeve; confirms the big-cash-pile thesis (real yields falling) even as equities wobbled Thursday.

items.headline: KOSPI's near-perfect 2-day round trip explained: chip-stock crash (Wed) then buyback-fueled rebound (Thu)
items.summary: KOSPI fell 5.80% Wed 19 Aug (Samsung -7.82%, SK Hynix -9.75%) on a US 30-year Treasury yield spike to a 19-year high plus a Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5% US selloff the prior session, triggering a program-sell halt. Thu 20 Aug it surged 5.89% (nearly erasing the drop) after Samsung and SK Hynix announced massive capital-return plans (>KRW100tn and ~KRW40tn respectively) and the Treasury buyback (item #1) eased bond-yield fears.
items.actionable: A leveraged, yield-driven chip-sector round trip, not a structural anomaly — a preview of how violently HK tech (Tencent/SMIC, similarly AI-capex-exposed) can swing on the same yield/AI-capex-jitters axis; treat single-day HSI/SMIC moves this week with the same lens.

items.headline: Gold/silver breakout driven by real-yield collapse and a weak dollar, not the FOMC minutes themselves
items.summary: Gold and silver rallied sharply (GLD +3.84%, SLV +4.47%) Wed 19 Aug as the Treasury buyback news pulled real yields down ahead of the FOMC minutes release, while a weaker dollar amplified gains for foreign buyers. Miners outperformed the metals (GDX +9.42%, SILJ +9.55%, Barrick +8.82%), consistent with a positioning/short-covering rally layered on the fundamental move.
items.actionable: Confirms this is a genuine rates/dollar-driven breakout, not a one-off headline spike — unlike Monday 17 Aug's futures-roll artifact that was corrected in the prior brief. Supports holding into further Fed dovish repricing, but Thursday's deceleration (GDX +2.59%) shows miners are now also correlating with broader equity risk-off.

items.headline: Thursday's US equity selloff (S&P -0.87%, VIX +7.52%) driven by AI-capex balance-sheet fears, not rates
items.summary: The WSJ flagged roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments across nine major tech names, reviving 'AI bubble' concerns even as the 30yr yield eased post-buyback. VIX jumped over 7% to 16.01 and the 10yr climbed toward 4.70% intraday. Rare-earth names caught in the same downdraft: MP Materials -2.89%, Energy Fuels -6.40%.
items.actionable: An AI-capex-credibility scare, structurally different from Wednesday's rates-driven metals rally — expect continued volatility in rare-earth/AI-adjacent names (MP, UUUU) independent of the gold/silver trend; staying out of AI-capex-linked equities near-term is consistent with the big-cash-pile positioning.

items.headline: July FOMC minutes lean hawkish: three regional presidents dissented for a hike, not a cut
items.summary: Minutes from the 28-29 July meeting (rates held at 3.50-3.75%) showed three regional Fed presidents (Logan, Hammack, Kashkari) dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, with the Committee focused on inflation persistence. New Fed Chair Warsh also floated moving to 6 meetings/year.
items.actionable: The metals rally happened despite hawkish minutes, purely on the Treasury buyback/liquidity story — a reminder the gold/silver trade is now a debt-monetization trade, decoupled from the Fed's own rate rhetoric. Don't expect the minutes' hawkishness to cap gold near-term.

items.headline: Bitcoin surges toward ~$74,859 on Treasury buyback, Trump crypto-reserve talk, and a record short squeeze
items.summary: Bitcoin rose ~7% Wed and continued to a ~$74,859 Friday pre-Asia level. The Treasury's buyback move was read as monetary debasement, fueling a 'digital gold' bid; Trump met crypto executives pushing the CLARITY Act and floated a US strategic Bitcoin reserve. Coincided with a record $2.7-3bn short-position liquidation cascade, the largest since 2021.
items.actionable: Bitcoin's move is a levered, liquidation-driven amplification of the same liquidity/debasement narrative driving gold — correlated risk, not a diversifier, for the precious-metals thesis this week. Next catalysts: the Sept 15 CLARITY Act vote and Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29).

items.headline: Iran conflict escalates: ADNOC tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Trump announces 'Operation Economic Fury'
items.summary: Two ADNOC vessels were attacked transiting the Strait of Hormuz Thu evening (one crew death). On Tue 19 Aug Trump announced sweeping new sanctions on Iran's oil, shipping and financial sectors plus a continued naval blockade, calling it 'the most crushing economic operation ever' against Iran.
items.actionable: A live, unresolved war-risk premium in both oil and gold — contributed to Tue/Wed's Asia risk-off and supports the gold safe-haven bid independent of the rates story. Monitor for a Hormuz closure escalation as a tail risk to HK tech/SGX shipping-adjacent names.

items.headline: Alibaba fiscal Q1: revenue beats, profit misses on 75% YoY AI capex surge; rare HK$10.4bn southbound outflow
items.summary: Alibaba reported revenue of RMB268.95bn (+9% YoY, beat) but adjusted net profit of RMB20.72bn missed estimates (vs RMB25.58bn expected) as capex hit RMB67.68bn (+75% YoY) on AI infrastructure spend. Mainland investors made contrarian net additions to Alibaba (HK$2.21bn) even as Hong Kong saw a rare HK$10.4bn single-day southbound net outflow.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-driven margin compression mirrors the US 'off-balance-sheet AI commitments' scare (item #4) playing out in HK tech — the contrarian mainland dip-buying is worth tracking as a read on HK tech risk appetite generally.

items.headline: Tencent Q2 capex up 176% YoY to RMB52.8bn on AI spend; shares +1.08% Wed to 447.20
items.summary: Tencent's capital expenditure surged 176% YoY to RMB52.8 billion as it ramps AI infrastructure investment, testing investor patience with the bullish thesis even as shares rose modestly Wed (+1.08% to HK$447.20, market cap $508.6bn) and continued higher Thu (+0.94% to 451.40).
items.actionable: Consistent with the broader AI-capex-scrutiny theme — HK tech capex intensity is now a two-sided risk (growth story vs margin/FCF concern); watch for further capex-driven volatility across the Hang Seng Tech complex.

items.headline: Singapore banks post record/near-record Q2 2026 profits; OCBC crosses S$30 for the first time
items.summary: DBS (S$3.08bn, +9%), OCBC (S$2.22bn, +22%, record) and UOB (S$1.48bn, +10%) all beat estimates, driven by fee/wealth-management income rather than lending margins. OCBC and DBS trade at all-time highs; UOB lags on NIM compression (1.74%, -8bp), cut fee-income guidance, and is divesting UOB Asset Management (announced 5 Aug).
items.actionable: SGX bank strength (OCBC/DBS momentum) is a structural positive for the owner's largest exposure sleeve independent of this week's volatility; UOB's relative weakness warrants closer monitoring versus peers.

items.headline: China's property crisis remains unresolved: Vanke posts combined 2-year loss over 130bn yuan
items.summary: State-linked developer China Vanke posted a record 89bn yuan annual loss (130bn yuan combined over two years); Evergrande remains delisted (worthless) since Aug 2025; restructured private developers face a fresh liquidity squeeze this year as the five-year downturn continues.
items.actionable: No new acute trigger this week, but a live structural overhang on HK-listed developers/banks with mainland property credit exposure — a background risk to monitor alongside the AI-capex-driven HK tech volatility rather than an immediate catalyst.

items.headline: Jackson Hole Symposium (27-29 Aug) — new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first keynote lands Fri 28 Aug
items.summary: Jackson Hole runs 27-29 Aug with Kevin Warsh delivering his first keynote as Fed Chair on Fri 28 Aug (official theme: payments, but labor-market weakness and inflation are expected to dominate). Lands 19 days before the 16 Sep FOMC decision.
items.actionable: The next major scheduled catalyst for gold/silver and rates — given Warsh's dissent history favored hikes over cuts, his tone could either validate or puncture the current liquidity/debasement rally in metals and Bitcoin. Size gold/silver-miner positioning with this event in mind.
